title: When do the ledgers meet?
hook: Compare a fictional fixed cost with a cost per query.

knows: Multiplication, division and units of energy
doesNotKnow: Training=100 kWh; serving=.01 kWh/query. At how many queries does serving equal training?

misconception: The contrasting operations must produce the same result.
objective: Compare the declared primary computation with its changed countercase and explain the boundary.

claims.text: Training=100 kWh; serving=.01 kWh/query. At how many queries does serving equal training? The locked stage supplies the declared finite operands and rules; computed outputs are hidden until commitment. Options: 1,000; 10,000; 20,000.
claims.source: Finite construction in company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30.md section 8; executable model.ts and model-check.mjs; builder provenance company/reviews/ai-energy-train-vs-serve/build.md. This supports the declared toy only; real-system literature acquisition and independent review remain pending.

claims.text: Your retained ledgers show serving 10 and total 110 at 1,000 queries, then serving 100 and total 200 at 10,000. Halving the query rate moved equal energy to 20,000 queries. Units are kWh, not money or carbon. Idle power, cooling, hardware and retraining are excluded; totals with different boundaries are not directly comparable. These are fictional amounts, not provider measurements.
claims.source: Finite construction in company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30.md section 8; executable model.ts and model-check.mjs; builder provenance company/reviews/ai-energy-train-vs-serve/build.md. claims.text: If the rate halves to .005 kWh/query while training stays 100 kWh, what is the crossover? 20,000 queries: 100/.005. Adding cooling to only one ledger would change its accounting boundary, so its total would no longer be directly comparable.
